cases.source_passage: In a voluntary pilot, 14 staff members reported that the checklist improved their perception of handoff clarity. Assignment was not randomized and the investigators explicitly did not estimate causes.
cases.claim_text: Fourteen pilot participants reported improved perceived handoff clarity, but the design did not establish that the checklist caused the change.
cases.gold_rationale: The source supports a reported perception and the claim explicitly refuses causal attribution.

cases.source_passage: In the comparison of the fictional units, the change in completion rates was not statistically significant. Confidence limits spanned both a small benefit and a small disadvantage.
cases.claim_text: The analysis did not establish a statistically significant improvement in completion rates between the units.
cases.gold_rationale: The negation of significance in the claim agrees with the source.

cases.source_passage: Within the high-volume subgroup, the median handling time fell from 16 to 9 days. Within the low-volume subgroup it rose from 10 to 12 days; no overall median was reported.
cases.claim_text: The median handling time decreased in the high-volume subgroup, while the low-volume subgroup showed the opposite pattern.
cases.gold_rationale: The claim explicitly attributes opposing directions to different subgroups.

cases.source_passage: The fictional evaluation covered only two municipal offices. All organizations included in that limited sample returned a completed questionnaire; other organizations were not approached.
cases.claim_text: All organizations in the two-office sample returned the questionnaire, without evidence about organizations outside that sample.
cases.gold_rationale: The universal quantifier is restricted to the sampled two offices.

cases.source_passage: Records for Unit C were missing and no outcomes were available for that unit. Analysts reported results only for Units A and B, both within one fictional region.
cases.claim_text: No improvement outcome can be assessed for Unit C because the source provides no Unit C results.
cases.gold_rationale: The claim accurately states an evidentiary absence, rather than an invented improvement.

cases.source_passage: Two drafts of the fictional meeting minutes listed different approval dates, 10 April and 12 April 2024. The discrepancy was unresolved, and the final decision date was not confirmed.
cases.claim_text: The documentary record does not establish a final approval date because the two versions conflict.
cases.gold_rationale: The claim preserves rather than conceals uncertainty over the date.

cases.source_passage: A structured survey of six clerks working in a single public archive reported occasional delays caused by the indexing screen. The report made no claims about other archives or government sectors.
cases.claim_text: The findings show a widespread pattern of indexing delays throughout public administration in the country.
cases.gold_rationale: A local signal is generalized to an unstudied national administration.

cases.source_passage: In the fictional case records, requests handled after a software redesign took less time. The group composition and workload differed across periods and no alternative explanations were assessed.
cases.claim_text: The software redesign was responsible for the faster processing observed in the later period.
cases.gold_rationale: Attribution of responsibility is causal even without using a trigger verb from the rule list.

cases.source_passage: Nine of the twelve employees who answered the fictional questionnaire indicated that the portal occasionally slowed their work. Forty colleagues were invited but did not answer.
cases.claim_text: Three quarters of the department's workforce experienced delays when using the portal.
cases.gold_rationale: The 9/12 respondent proportion cannot be extended to the unobserved workforce.

cases.source_passage: The fictional prototype correctly categorized 29 of 30 artificially generated procurement requests in a supervised offline exercise. The authors did not test actual procurement cases or changing legal rules.
cases.claim_text: The prototype is ready for dependable use in authentic procurement operations involving current regulations.
cases.gold_rationale: Success on artificial requests alone does not justify deployment readiness.

cases.source_passage: In the fictional experiment, one subgroup showed a small gain in accuracy while two others showed no measurable change. The authors did not calculate a pooled effectiveness estimate.
cases.claim_text: Accuracy improved consistently throughout the participating workforce after the procedural change.
cases.gold_rationale: The claim discards non-improving subgroups and generalizes one signal.

cases.source_passage: Five interviewees described difficulty finding uploaded records. The interviews were exploratory and the authors provided neither prevalence estimates nor a probability sample.
cases.claim_text: The majority of administrators face difficulty finding records on the platform.
cases.gold_rationale: The prevalence claim cannot be established by five exploratory testimonies.

cases.source_passage: In the fictional committee minutes, seven members opposed the proposal and two supported it. The chair recorded the motion as defeated after the vote.
cases.claim_text: The committee endorsed the proposal by a substantial majority after deliberation.
cases.gold_rationale: The documented outcome was rejection, whereas the claim asserts endorsement.

cases.source_passage: The hypothetical ministry documented an unapproved software concept. No operational deployment, field trial, or user training had occurred by the date of the report.
cases.claim_text: The ministry had already launched the system and trained administrative staff to use it in routine work.
cases.gold_rationale: The source explicitly rules out the claimed launch and training.

cases.source_passage: The fictional examinations showed mean accuracy of 62 points before training and 48 points afterward. These are the only accuracy observations described.
cases.claim_text: Average accuracy was higher after training than before it, according to the examination record.
cases.gold_rationale: The direction of the 62 to 48 change is opposite the claim, expressed without a trigger word.

cases.source_passage: The fictional comparison relied entirely on manually sorted correspondence. Neither predictive software nor machine-learning classification formed part of the methods.
cases.claim_text: An automated classifier produced the grouping decisions used in the experiment.
cases.gold_rationale: The source describes fully manual grouping, not automation.

cases.source_passage: The archival sample consisted exclusively of state-owned enterprises. Privately controlled firms were outside the sampling frame and were not represented.
cases.claim_text: Private firms were a substantial part of the sampled organizations in the archival study.
cases.gold_rationale: The claimed sampled population did not exist in the reported sampling frame.

cases.source_passage: The fictional ethics committee determined that the submitted proposal required substantial revision and should not proceed to recruitment at that time.
cases.claim_text: The ethics committee cleared the proposal to begin recruitment without further revision.
cases.gold_rationale: The source denies the alleged permission to start recruiting.

cases.source_passage: The authors described a future randomized test of a revised service form, but the protocol did not include any observations and recruitment had yet to begin.
cases.claim_text: The revised service form proved effective at preventing incomplete applications in the pilot agencies.
cases.gold_rationale: No results are available from a not-yet-conducted test.

cases.source_passage: The fictional project report listed 12 completed training sessions but did not measure subsequent job performance, adherence to procedure, or participant competence.
cases.claim_text: The sessions left employees substantially more competent in their daily responsibilities.
cases.gold_rationale: Session counts provide no basis for a claimed competence gain.

cases.source_passage: A system outage prevented extraction of Unit D records, so the fictional report offered no Unit D backlog figures for either quarter. Only Units A to C were included.
cases.claim_text: Unit D had eliminated its backlog by the end of the second quarter.
cases.gold_rationale: There are no observed backlog outcomes for Unit D.

cases.source_passage: One anonymous comment suggested that service users might prefer the redesigned notice. There were no structured interviews or before-and-after satisfaction measurements.
cases.claim_text: The redesigned notice was preferred by service users overall compared with the prior format.
cases.gold_rationale: The single anonymous comment cannot establish an overall preference.

cases.source_passage: Two independently generated inventory files assigned different dates to the supposed asset transfer. The original signed transfer record was unavailable to the review team.
cases.claim_text: The asset was formally transferred on 6 June 2024 in the documented transaction.
cases.gold_rationale: No authoritative signed record settles the transfer date.

cases.source_passage: The fictional quarterly report recorded 51 completed requests during one quarter, but no earlier quarter's figures were available and the definition of completion had changed.
cases.claim_text: The office achieved better throughput than in the preceding quarter using an unchanged metric.
cases.gold_rationale: The comparator and consistent denominator needed for this trend claim are absent.
